data.name: Daksh
data.gender_notes: Daksh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Daksh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Dakshina', which means 'right-handed' or 'the god of wealth and prosperity'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Daksh is the divine being who represents the power of wealth and prosperity. This name is believed to bring good luck, wealth and prosperity to the one who bears it. The name Daksh carries the meaning “God of Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Daksh usually hope their child will grow to embody god of prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine energy of abundance and prosperity, and is believed to bless the bearer with wealth, success, and prosperity in all areas of life.
data.etymology: Daksh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Daksh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The word 'Daksh' comes from the Sanskrit root 'daks' which means 'to reach' or 'to touch'. The prefix 'da' in 'Daksh' denotes 'great' or 'excellent'. Hence, the name Daksh means 'the one who is dexterous, skilled or able'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Indra, the God of Rain, is also known as Daksh. He is often depicted as the God of sacrifice and is also considered as the God of wealth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Daksh carries a significant cultural impact as it is derived from 'Dakshina', a term deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and rituals. Dakshina refers to an offering or a donation made to a deity or a priest, symbolizing respect and gratitude. Thus, the name Daksh signifies wealth, generosity, and prosperity within the Hindu cultural context.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Daksh holds deep symbolism as it represents Lord Daksh, the divine being associated with the power of wealth and prosperity. This name is believed to bring good fortune, protect the bearer from financial instability, and ensure Overall Well-being. Additionally, it is considered a powerful name for those seeking success in material aspects of life. By invoking the blessings of Lord Daksh, individuals are encouraged to share their resources generously and create abundance not only for themselves but also for their loved ones and community.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Daksh symbolizes the embodiment of sacrifice and virtuous conduct. In Hindu mythology, Lord Daksh is known for conducting a yajna (sacrifice) where he invited all gods except Lord Shiva. This act led to the wrath of Shiva, resulting in the destruction of the yajna. Despite this, Daksh is revered for his unwavering devotion to the gods and the purifying power of his yajna.

vedic_reference.note: In Hindu mythology, Lord Indra, the God of Rain, is also known as Daksh.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Daksha Prajapati was the father of Sati, the consort of Lord Shiva. When Daksha organised a yajna (sacrifice) and intentionally excluded Shiva, Sati was deeply hurt and immolated herself.
Daksha is also mentioned in the Rigveda, the oldest existing text of Hinduism, as a priest performing rituals and hymns in honor of various gods and goddesses.

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
